messages:
emily-cs: FYI — Acme Corp flagged a mismatch between the dashboard and their finalized invoice for Jan. They say dashboard shows 1.2M tokens, invoice charged 1.38M. Can someone take a look? :thinking:
raj-finance: Ack — do we have the invoice id and the account id? invoice id  INV-2026-01-908, account acme-corp-42?
emily-cs: Yep invoice INV-2026-01-908, account acme-corp-42. Customer says totals differ by ~180K tokens and one plan line moved from "standard" to "standard+burst" on the invoice.
marco-support: Putting on my list. Quick Q: dashboard time window was local TZ or UTC? month-close cutoff changes have bitten us before.
emily-cs: Customer screenshot shows dashboard window as "Jan 1 — Jan 31 (UTC)". They do a manual export CSV and still see 1.2M.
raj-finance: I'll pull the invoice render. billing-bot, can you attach the token rollup for INV-2026-01-908?
billing-bot: Attached token-rollup CSV (summary rows): account=acme-corp-42, invoice_total_tokens=1380452, dashboard_export_tokens=1202120, line_items=[standard:850000, standard+burst:530452]
emily-cs: Huh — so invoice split shows 530K on standard+burst, but customer claims they were on standard whole month.
olivia-prodeng: Quick hypothesis: a late backfill/embedding job completed after cutoff and was billed to invoice window because our background aggregator used ingestion timestamp instead of completed_at. Can you share job logs?
marco-support: Reproducing — I queried usage_events table for acme-corp-42 around midnight Jan 31 -> Feb 1. SQL I ran: 
```
SELECT event_type, token_count, created_at, ingested_at, processed_at
FROM usage_events
WHERE account = 'acme-corp-42' AND created_at >= '2026-01-31'::timestamptz AND created_at < '2026-02-01'::timestamptz
ORDER BY created_at;
```
I see ~180K tokens with created_at 2026-01-31 23:59:50 UTC but processed_at 2026-02-01 00:03:10 UTC.
raj-finance: If created_at is in Jan, invoice should include them. But customer says dashboard excluded them — maybe the dashboard export filters on processed_at.
emily-cs: Customer insists they did not run any bulk backfills. They use standard tier; no burst config.
olivia-prodeng: Can you paste the worker log snippet for that backfill job id? I want to confirm origin.
marco-support: Log snippet: 
```
2026-02-01T00:02:55Z worker-12 INFO backfill job_id=bf-9876 started for account=acme-corp-42
2026-02-01T00:03:10Z worker-12 INFO backfill job_id=bf-9876 processed 179482 tokens in 35s
2026-02-01T00:03:30Z worker-12 INFO backfill job_id=bf-9876 finished
```
marco-support: Looks like the job created usage events with created_at set to original message timestamps (31st) but processing and ingestion happened a few minutes into Feb. Dashboard export pipeline uses processed_at filter for month window; invoice/ledger uses created_at.
raj-finance: That would explain total delta and plan tier bump: the token spike was large enough to push them into burst pricing for invoice calculation (our aggregator applies tier based on token thresholds inside invoice window).
emily-cs: Customer will be unhappy. What are remediation options?
olivia-prodeng: Short term: we can issue a one-time invoice adjustment/credit for tokens that were processed after cutoff if customer confirms they weren't running backfills. But we should patch aggregator to use consistent windowing (created_at vs processed_at).
marco-support: I'll tag SRE to check worker backfill scheduling — why did job run at 00:02 UTC. Could be cron drift.
raj-finance: Approving a credit for the 179,482 tokens as a gesture; finance will document a memo. Emily, can you check with Acme whether they triggered bf-9876? If they didn't, we issue credit and set follow-up with product for windowing change.
emily-cs: On it. I'll DM the customer and update thread. Thanks all :heart:
raj-finance: Adding final note — ticket #FIN-5421 for the adjustment and a linked engineering task ENG-1209 for aggregator fix.
marco-support: I'll append reproducer and SQL snippets to ENG-1209.
